case_title: Gurdip Singh v. State of Punjab
high_court_outcome: Maintained conviction but reduced sentence under Section 3048
neutral_facts: The accused, a father-in-law, and his son, the husband, were involved in the case. The deceased, a married woman, was subjected to harassment and cruelty by both accused, including demands for dowry. The deceased was sent out of her matrimonial home due to these pressures. The deceased's body was found in her home, and there were allegations of poisoning. The prosecution claimed that the accused had threatened to kill her if she did not meet dowry demands. The trial court convicted both accused under Sections 498A and 3048 of the IPC, while the High Court reduced the sentence under Section 3048. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction under Section 498A but set aside the conviction under Section 3048 due to insufficient evidence regarding the death occurring within seven years of marriage.
